dt-example.title: Search parameter (id matching)
dt-example.info:
StateRestore has the ability to provide bookmarking support for states - i.e. when a page is loaded, StateRestore will check the URL to see if there is a specific state that should be loaded. This allows:
1. Links to be provided to a table in a specific state 2. The end user can load a state and then bookmark that URL for reloading at another time. The table will be restored in that state.
Bookmarking in StateRestore is not enabled by default, but is easily configured using the `-init stateRestore.bookmark` configuration object - specifically the `src` property must be set. This parameter tells StateRestore if it should look in the query / search parameters, or the URI hash for the state to be loaded.
In this case, `-init stateRestore.bookmark.src` is set to be `?dtsr`. The `?` tells the software that it will be a query parameter and the following part is the parameter name (`dtsr` in this case).
By default the state `id` is the property that the match will be performed on (although this is configurable with `-init stateRestore.bookmark.match`), so `?dtsr=1` will load state id 1, etc.
The following links demonstrate that for the three predefined states in this example:
* [Search - London](?dtsr=1) * [Order - Position](?dtsr=2) * [Search and order](?dtsr=3)
Click the links and the page will reload with the selected state. Obviously, if you were linking to a state on the same page, you would actually just use `-api state()` or `-api stateRestore.state().load()` to prevent the full refresh - this is just an example to show how external links might work.
Next: [State name matching](./searchName).
